w: Perched on the Florentinerberg, this castle was seat of the Margraves of Baden from the late 15th century, then the Margraves of Baden-Baden from 1535 to the 17th's end. Rebuilt and extended repeatedly since its medieval origins, the listed building is now owned by Kuwaiti investors planning a luxury-hotel conversion.
s: A margraves' seat now bound for a luxury hotel
_facts: Seat of the Margraves of Baden from the late 15th century
Seat of the Margraves of Baden-Baden from 1535 to the end of the 17th century
Rebuilt and extended several times since its Late Middle Ages origins
Now owned by Kuwaiti investors planning a luxury-hotel conversion

w: This 2.3-kilometre riverside avenue began around 1655 as a path from the town market to Lichtenthal monastery, then was replanted from 1850 to 1870 on the orders of casino director Benazet with some 300 species of trees and shrubs. It ends in a dahlia garden holding busts of Clara Schumann, Brahms and Robert Stolz.
s: A promenade ending in a garden of Brahms busts
_facts: 2.3 km strolling avenue along the river Oos
Began around 1655 as a path to Lichtenthal monastery
Replanted 1850-1870 at the instigation of the casino Benazet, with about 300 plant species
Ends in a dahlia garden with busts of Clara Schumann, Brahms and Robert Stolz

w: Known locally as Lichtental No. 8, this Baden-Baden house is now a biographical museum to Johannes Brahms, built around the attic room where the composer actually lived and worked on his music during his stays in the spa town.
s: The attic where Brahms composed, now a museum
_facts: Also known as Lichtental No. 8
Biographical museum dedicated to Johannes Brahms
Centred on the attic where Brahms lived and worked while in residence

w: Built in 1961 on the 525-metre Fremersberg above Baden-Baden, this 83-metre reinforced-concrete telecommunications tower carries an observation deck 30 metres up. A small restaurant sits alongside it, a modest reward for the climb up the hill on the edge of the Black Forest.
s: An 83-metre tower with a view and a snack bar
_facts: Built 1961, 83 metres tall, reinforced concrete
Observation deck 30 metres above ground
Sits on the 525-metre Fremersberg near Baden-Baden
Small restaurant next to the tower

w: South of Baden-Baden's Geroldsau district, the Grobbach stream drops about six metres into a small rock bowl to form this waterfall. The stream rises on the rainy western slopes of the northern Black Forest, merging with the Harzbach just upstream, and averages a modest 0.56 cubic metres a second even here.
s: A six-metre waterfall in the Black Forest
_facts: About 6 metres high, on the Grobbach stream
South of Baden-Baden's Geroldsau quarter, northern Black Forest
Grobbach merges with the Harzbach just above the falls
Average flow of about 0.56 cubic metres per second

w: These ruins above Baden-Baden are what remains of Schloss Eberstein, built in 1100 as the main seat of the Counts of Eberstein. By the late 16th century the family had abandoned it and much of the stone was carted off. What survives is now a national monument and a State Palace of Baden-Wuerttemberg.
s: A count's 1100 castle, stripped for its stone
_facts: Original structure built 1100
Primary residence of the Counts of Eberstein
Abandoned by the end of the 16th century; much torn down for materials
Now a German national monument and State Palace of Baden-Wuerttemberg

w: Standing on the Merkur hill since 8 April 1950, this observation tower began life transmitting FM radio for broadcaster SWF, adding television from 1953. It gained a new 23-metre tower between 1980 and 1982, topped by a 40-metre aerial mast, with a lift for visitors chasing the view over Baden-Baden.
s: A 1950 radio tower you can ride to the top
_facts: In use as an FM-radio transmission tower since 8 April 1950 (SWF, now SWR)
Added television transmission from 1953
New 23-metre tower built 1980-1982 with a 40-metre aerial mast
Includes a visitor lift
